passage.passage_text:
In the heart of the Pacific Ocean, an unwelcome spectacle named the Great Pacific Garbage Patch swirls, an alarming testament to human carelessness. This vast collection of marine debris, predominantly resilient plastics, floats and degrades slowly, highlighting the severe issue of plastic pollution in our oceans. Our daily reliance on plastic items, from water bottles to shopping bags, combined with improper disposal, is the primary cause of this escalating problem.

The journey of plastic in the ocean is a distressing one. Over time, the resilient plastic breaks down into smaller pieces under the harsh sun and the constant churning of the waves. These tiny fragments, called microplastics, become abundant in the waters, almost invisible to the naked eye, but not to the marine life that mistakenly consumes them. The harmful effects of plastic pollution vary across marine species. For instance, sea turtles may mistake floating plastic bags for jellyfish, their favorite meal, leading to fatal consequences. Meanwhile, smaller creatures like plankton ingest microplastics, which then accumulate up the food chain, affecting larger marine animals and ultimately, humans.

Summarizing, the issue of plastic pollution poses a significant threat to our oceans and the diverse life they support. If left unchecked, the future implications are grave. Marine species could face extinction, our seafood could become contaminated, and the balance of the entire marine ecosystem could be irreversibly disrupted. However, there are potential solutions to this daunting issue. We can reduce our use of single-use plastics, improve waste management systems, and support clean-up efforts in our oceans.

The tale of plastic pollution is a stark reminder of the cause-effect relationship between human actions and the health of our planet. It's a story of how something as resilient and abundant as plastic can turn into a menacing invader in our oceans, threatening the survival of countless marine species, and eventually, our own.

recall_scoring.general_instructions: For each sentence, award 2 points if student recalls BOTH the character and key detail, 1 point for either one, 0 points for neither. Allow paraphrasing.
recall_scoring.passage_title: Title: The Resilient Invaders: Plastic Pollution in Our Oceans

student_action: Phase 1 - Reading: Student reads the passage silently or aloud (as appropriate) from beginning to end. Student may take as much time as needed to read and understand the passage. Phase 2 - Recall: After reading, passage is removed/covered. Student orally recalls everything they remember from the passage. Student may include characters, events, details, and main ideas. Assessor records recalled sentences. Phase 3 - Questions: Passage is made visible again. Student answers multiple-choice comprehension questions (typically 5-6 questions). Student may refer back to the passage while answering questions. Student selects answer choice (A, B, or C).
assessor_grading: Assessor scores in three phases: Phase 1 - Reading: Observe and note reading behaviors, fluency, and any difficulties (not formally scored but noted). Phase 2 - Recall: For each sentence in the passage, assessor marks if student recalled: (1) the character/subject mentioned in sentence, (2) the key detail/action in sentence. Each sentence receives 2 points (both recalled), 1 point (one recalled), or 0 points (neither recalled). Total recall score = sum of sentence scores. Recall accuracy ratio = total points / max possible points. Phase 3 - Questions: Assessor marks each multiple-choice question as CORRECT (correct answer selected) or INCORRECT (wrong answer, multiple selections, or no response). Question score = total correct out of total questions. Overall comprehension performance combines both recall accuracy and question accuracy.

assessor_script: SETUP: Prepare assessment materials. Ensure student has access to passage and questions.

• Allow student to read passage at their own pace
• Present questions one at a time
• Mark each answer as correct or incorrect
